body:
I generally agree with all you said :100:

I just want to point out that some example apps are not in a "shareable" state (i.e. this is not just a matter of adding the `<live-example>` tag in all guides). Some example apps need work in order to be helpful as standalone example apps. (Fortunately, that only applies to few of them, but we should check case-by-case when adding `<live-example>` tags.)

Yes, this is true! Thank you, @gkalpak, for making sure it is pointed out. For whoever picks it up (if it's not me! 😁), the `<live-example>` tags can't just be added to all docs. When we go through, we'll need to look at a case by case basis to determine the scope as some will be a greater level of effort than others. We also need to make sure that it makes sense in the context of each doc and check that all the included `<code-example>` tags still make sense. This would be best done in a number of smaller PRs rather than one big one.
Wow, sure, @ajitsinghkaler! It may be helpful to do them in small PRs, one doc at a time. I imagine that this issue would take one PR or more for each of the points above. Does that help? Thank you!
@ajitsinghkaler Just wondering if you are working on this. If not, I can help out.
@kapunahelewong The first link is missing the `s` in the end. It should be `https://angular.io/guide/dependency-injection-providers`
I'm on a holiday for 10 days and I'll only start working on it after that you can start working on this. No problem
@ajitsinghkaler Sounds good. I can create a few PRs for it and we can probably split the work when you are back.

@kapunahelewong / @gkalpak How about taking this one step further and we display a download icon next to the pencil icon in the top right corner of the content. 

Something like this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/59734/76612229-3c044f00-64f2-11ea-941c-f901798744de.png)

This will be cleaner and help us to avoid creating new content sections that basically would just say "Download accompanying code from here". 

WDYT?
